clue.text: Accept a hand is to be dismissed

definitions.meaning: to take the cards dealt to you in a card game
British idiom for being sacked, from the employment documents handed back to a departing worker

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an employee's cards (national insurance papers) were returned on dismissal, so this phrase meant being fired; read literally it is simply picking up a dealt hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means losing your job, and literally it describes taking up the cards dealt in a game.

clue.text: Grass edges round forest providing recreation areas

indicators.note: the outer letters go round the forest, enclosing it
the edges of the word grass are its first and last letters

parts.note: Arden is a forest in Warwickshire, the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: Lawn borders surrounding woodland supplying places to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges' takes G and S, the first and last letters of 'Grass', and 'round' wraps them about ARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Public parks and pleasure grounds are places for leisure and recreation.

clue.text: Being a little wet is in bad taste

definitions.meaning: slightly sticky, as paint not yet dry

explanation.definitionFit: Paint still slightly sticky is described this way, as is something cheap and vulgar.

clue.text: Chief's record currently unsurpassed

definitions.meaning: the person in charge, the boss
a single at the top of the charts

explanation.definitionFit: The boss is called this, and so is the single at the top of the charts.

clue.text: Murdered — there's a twist

definitions.meaning: past tense of slay, to kill

explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of slay means killed, and as a noun the word means a sideways turn or swing.

clue.text: Those who see the programme for royal reception

definitions.meaning: the viewers or spectators of a show
a formal interview granted by a monarch

explanation.definitionFit: The spectators of a show, and a formal meeting granted by a sovereign or the Pope.

clue.text: Lifeboat apparatus lacked a vital part

indicators.note: only part of the words lacked a vital is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A lifeboat's machinery missing an essential component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' picks out the run inside lackeD A VITal.
explanation.definitionFit: A davit is the small crane used to lower and raise a ship's lifeboat.

clue.text: During fresh rising. I had to be fearless

parts.note: in means during, as in in the night

indicators.note: in a down clue a word rising is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: pert means cheeky, fresh
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Bold new recruits come up through the ranks, needing courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' is a down-clue reversal signal; the full stop after it is surface punctuation, and the printed 'he' is an OCR slip for 'be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means dauntless and brave.

clue.text: Decided to go down in the record

indicators.note: one word set within another, as the clue's in says

parts.note: a CD, compact disc, is a record
to lose is to go down to defeat

explanation.surface: A ruling to sink is entered into the minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that is closed is settled, finally decided.

clue.text: Advise newcomer how to get things right

indicators.note: the first part of the word newcomer tells us the rest of it is made new, rearranged

parts.note: to mend is to put things right, repair them

explanation.surface: Telling someone who has just arrived how to sort things out.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'newcomer' does double duty as two pieces: its first three letters are the anagram signal for the rest; 'how to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To recommend a course is to advise someone to take it.

clue.text: Nitrogen injected into meat it's easy to buy

indicators.note: something injected goes inside, so the nitrogen symbol is placed within the meat

parts.note: veal is calf meat
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A butcher pumping nitrogen into cheap meat that is easy to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a person or official who can be bought, i.e. bribed, rather than a cheap product.
explanation.definitionFit: Venal describes someone open to bribery, whose loyalty can readily be purchased.

clue.text: Palace in two dioceses

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city whose diocese is in Cambridgeshire
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A bishop's palace that straddles a pair of dioceses.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is an English cathedral city and diocese; the second diocese is the general word for one. The answer is the French President's palace in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Élysée is the Paris residence of the President of France, a palace.

clue.text: Bits of paper abandoned after use

indicators.note: letters that are abandoned are left wild and disorderly, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scraps of paper thrown away once they have served their purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bits of paper' suggests scraps being thrown away, but it means regular sections of a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper articles beyond the news pages, such as profiles and reviews, are its regular sections or pieces.

clue.text: Area where men follow cult

indicators.note: the men come after the cult in the answer, as the word follow directs

parts.note: a sect is a religious cult or faction
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers, men as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A place where men are followers of a cult.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct zone or district.

clue.text: Pot, tin and basin mixed up

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: the letters of basin are jumbled, mixed up

explanation.surface: Kitchenware muddled together: a pot, a tin and a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like kitchenware alongside tin and basin but is slang for the drug; 'mixed up' rearranges BASIN to NABIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for marijuana.

clue.text: Exchanged blows, namely hit sharply

parts.note: SC, short for Latin scilicet, means namely
rapped means struck smartly

explanation.surface: Someone describing a fight in which punches were traded and landed hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap is to fight, so having scrapped is having traded punches.

clue.text: Loss of 25 may develop in age, alas

indicators.note: letters that develop change form, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting losses that come with getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25 down, agony. 'may develop' rearranges IN AGE ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the absence of the sensation of agony, as brought about by painkillers.

clue.text: Note wife shortly is to get little boy for adoption

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: said shortly, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a spouse is a wife or husband
Al is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A wife about to take in a young boy as her own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts SPOUSE to SPOUS; 'is to get' simply joins the pieces. Adoption here is taking up a cause, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal of a cause or idea is taking it up and supporting it.

clue.text: Study some scripture and discuss

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a verse is a small portion of scripture

explanation.surface: Reading a passage of the Bible and then talking it over.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk together, a synonym of discuss.

clue.text: Two groups of officers see the world

parts.note: COs are commanding officers
MOs are medical officers

explanation.surface: Two sets of military officers travelling around the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: COs are commanding officers and MOs medical officers; 'see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos is the universe, the whole ordered world.

clue.text: Cut despicable worm

parts.note: a cad is a despicable man
to dis is to snub or cut someone

explanation.surface: Slicing up a nasty worm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb acting on the worm, but it is slang for snubbing someone, and it comes second in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The caddis worm is the larva of the caddis fly, used as fishing bait.

clue.text: Smoothly conniving about capsized boat

indicators.note: conniving goes about the boat, surrounding it

parts.note: sly means conniving, scheming

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue it is reversed

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed boat, a barge

explanation.surface: Someone scheming smoothly over an overturned boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A keel can be a flat-bottomed barge as well as the spine of a hull; 'capsized' turns it over and 'about' wraps the scheming word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleekly means in a smooth, glossy manner.

clue.text: Picture result of implementing short-term aim?

definitions.meaning: a shot fired quickly without taking careful aim

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into a quick shot fired after only a moment's aiming.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual photograph taken quickly is a common sense of the word, and literally it is a hurried shot.

clue.text: A flurry of shots beginning to send Oval wild

indicators.note: the beginning of send is its first letter
the letters of oval go wild, rearranged

explanation.surface: A burst of fire at the start that sends the Oval crowd wild.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground. 'beginning' takes S; 'wild' rearranges OVAL to ALVO.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a burst of fire.

clue.text: Tycoon's lost a million, it is related

indicators.note: the tycoon losing something means a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a magnate is a tycoon; the 's is the link 'has'
M is the abbreviation for a million

explanation.surface: A business baron has lost a million and it hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnate means related through the male line of descent, a kinsman on the father's side.

clue.text: Spirit, aged in wood for twelve years

definitions.meaning: an airy sprite in Shakespeare's The Tempest

definitions.text: aged in wood for twelve years
definitions.meaning: in The Tempest the witch Sycorax imprisoned this sprite in a cloven pine for twelve years

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading pretends to be a whisky matured in casks; it refers to Shakespeare's sprite trapped in a pine tree by Sycorax.
explanation.definitionFit: The airy sprite who serves Prospero in The Tempest had been trapped in a tree for twelve years.

clue.text: Old man experiencing agony

parts.note: pa is father, the old man
in means going through, as in in trouble

explanation.surface: An elderly father suffering terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is suffering, and agony is extreme suffering.

clue.text: College may be highly illuminating

definitions.meaning: a bay window projecting from an upper floor, letting in light high up

explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is an Oxford college; the second reading is an upper-storey bay window.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel College in Oxford, and an oriel window that lights a room from high on a wall.

clue.text: Taking over marble hall for games

parts.note: in cricket a bowler takes an over of six balls, so bowling
an alley is a large glass or alabaster marble

explanation.surface: Seizing control of a marble-floored hall used for games.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket, delivered by the bowler. 'Taking over' looks like seizing control but means bowling one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowling alley is a building where tenpin is played, a games venue.
